root_causes.description: The recommendation service exhibits extreme server-side latency: its p99 is saturated at the 10000ms histogram ceiling and its request traces run ~15s while reporting zero errors. This latency propagates upstream to frontend and checkout, which both depend on recommendation, producing the cluster-wide P99 latency watchdog alert.

evidence.expected_baseline: recommendation p99 in low-tens of ms; healthy peer cart p99 observed at 4.015ms

evidence.observed_value: 20 traces, 0 with errors, p95_duration=15759ms; top spans user_get_recommendations 15001ms (ok), 199ccde8385eca3a 15005ms (ok), user_browse_product 15000ms (ok)
evidence.expected_baseline: recommendation spans in low tens of ms with no >5s outliers
healthy sibling downstream of checkout - confirms anomaly is isolated, not cluster-wide saturation
no error logs - consistent with a pure latency fault rather than errors

root_causes.description: checkout's p99 is pinned at the 10000ms ceiling while its CPU usage is normal (~0.025 cores) and its error rate is negligible (~0.011), indicating checkout is being slowed by a slow downstream dependency (recommendation/product-catalog path) rather than intrinsic CPU or error-driven failure.

evidence.expected_baseline: checkout p99 should be low-tens of ms in normal operation
no CPU spike - rules out cpu_stress as the cause of checkout latency
error rate near zero - fault is latency, not an error/abort spike

root_causes.description: frontend's p99 is also pinned at the 10000ms ceiling, but as the top-level orchestrator calling both checkout and recommendation its latency is most plausibly propagation of the downstream slowdown rather than an intrinsic frontend fault.

evidence.expected_baseline: frontend p99 should track healthy downstreams (low-tens of ms)
no error logs - latency propagation rather than an error fault

remediation_steps: Investigate and scale out the recommendation deployment (increase replicas / CPU headroom) to relieve the saturated request handling producing ~15s traces.
Instrument the recommendation -> product-catalog call path with downstream client-span latency to confirm whether recommendation is blocked on a slow product-catalog dependency.
Check recommendation pod resource limits for CPU throttling and compare CPU usage vs. limits during the 08:02-08:04 UTC window.
Add client-side timeouts and circuit breakers on frontend and checkout calls to recommendation/high-latency dependencies to prevent P99 latency propagation cluster-wide.
Review recent flagd feature-flag and configuration changes affecting recommendation behavior during the incident window.
